title: Linux containment step 1: report containment from a probe, not a PATH lookup

AC4.note: probe.test.ts: 29 tests over an injected spawn. Failure reports the launcher stderr verbatim (bwrap: setting up uid map: Permission denied, only the trailing newline trimmed); success returns {layer,ok} with no detail, cause or remediation. Control characters stripped and output capped, asserted on bytes.

AC5.note: probeContainment caches process-globally: 3 calls, 1 spawn; cache holds across differing options. Falsifiable counterpart proves runContainmentProbe spawns every time. Wiring proven separately in sandbox.test.ts by priming the cache and asserting buildSandboxReport reuses it (spawns stays 1) — the composition a cacheProbe boolean had made untestable.

AC6.note: sandbox.test.ts: 29 tests, platform/launcher/probe/kernel injected. No row reads available unless the probe confirmed it AND the trial exercised it (coveredByProbe -> the unprobed finding). Linux unavailable reason names the kernel release and the withheld facility, never the string linux, and only when the probe identified a userns cause. Live-verified both ways on Ubuntu 24.04 kernel 6.8.0-136-generic via the injectable seam.

AC7.note: capability-matrix.doc-sync.test.ts: 13 tests iterating CAPABILITY_STATUSES, so a fourth state cannot be added and left undocumented. Falsifiability was fixed after a reviewer mutation proved the original 'falsifiable' cases were tautologies: the replacement doctors the parsed section and asserts the same filter now reports the state missing. A separate runbook-sync test in sandbox.test.ts covers the fifth user-visible finding (unprobed), which the matrix-only test could not see.

AC8.note: adapter.ts, wrap.ts, bwrap.ts, seatbelt.ts and profile.ts are absent from the full branch diff (git diff --name-only, empty). Escape hatches untouched: KERYX_DANGEROUSLY_DISABLE_SANDBOX and KERYX_SANDBOX_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED live in harness.ts and shell-exec-tool.ts, neither in the diff. Fail-closed tests unmodified and green. Verified independently in review rounds 2-6.

AC12.note: install.sh delegates to the keryx it just installed. install-global.test.ts: 12 pass. Shims cover absent bwrap, a bwrap that fails with the uid-map error (verbatim quote + AppArmor remediation, no sysctl), and one that contains. Plus the fail-safe branch (a keryx that cannot start claims nothing, either way, and still exits 0), the project-install delegation shape, three hostile TMPDIRs, and a noisy failing keryx asserted on bytes. Both bash tests falsified by hand.

AC13.note: PARTIAL, deliberately, and recorded rather than silently confirmed. R8's substance holds: no rendering path, output string or test fixture names the sysctl as a remedy, enforced by four not.toContain assertions (probe.test.ts, sandbox.test.ts, capability-matrix.doc-sync.test.ts, install-global.test.ts). All 15 repo mentions are rejections, statements of the kernel default, or negative assertions. The frozen wording also forbids COMMENTS from naming it; three comments introduced here do, each while explaining why ADR-0010 rejected it. Flagged by review rounds 4-6; the AC's letter is unmet, its intent is met and enforced.

AC14.note: No new npm dependency (package.json absent from the diff). purity.test.ts enforces N3 by test rather than by diff inspection: the pure modules cannot spawn directly or transitively (fixed-point closure over relative imports, so the barrel route is covered), matching import statements rather than substrings so a doc comment cannot trip it and cannot satisfy it. probe.ts performs no spawn when its seam is injected. Writing the guard found a real fact: tls-ca.ts also spawns, so the spawning set is computed from source rather than hand-maintained.
